newsitem.title: USA: NBA-SHAQ SCORES 42 AS LAKERS STAY ON SEATTLE'S HEELS.
newsitem.headline: NBA-SHAQ SCORES 42 AS LAKERS STAY ON SEATTLE'S HEELS.

text.p: After missing a big chunk of the season with a serious knee injury, Shaquille O'Neal is back in a big way and the rest of the Western Conference contenders had better prepare for a post-season "Shaq Attack."
O'Neal continued his torrid scoring spree since returning from injury by pouring in a season-high 42 points as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings 108-99 on Thursday.
The Lakers have won all three games since O'Neal's return to the lineup and he is averaging 35 points per game in that span. O'Neal also pulled down a game-high 12 rebounds.
Elden Campbell added 21 for Los Angeles, who kept pace with Seattle by staying a half game behind the Sonics in the battle for first place in the Pacific Division.
The Lakers have two games left, while Seattle has just one game to go in the regular season.
Mitch Richmond scored 23 points and Brian Grant added 19 for the Kings, who were swept by the Lakers this season.
In Denver, Shawn Kemp had 27 points and 12 rebounds and Sam Perkins hit a go-ahead three-pointer in the final minute as the Seattle SuperSonics beat the Nuggets 108-104.
Gary Payton scored 24 points and Detlef Schrempf added 18 for the Sonics, who stayed a half game ahead of the Lakers for first place in the Pacific Division.
Antonio McDyess scored 29 points and Dale Ellis added 27 for the Nuggets, who tied the game at 103-103 on Ervin Johnson's layup with two minutes left.

Denver had a chance to grab the lead, but Anthony Goldwire missed a pair of free throws with 72 seconds to play. Perkins then buried a three-pointer with 48 seconds left to put Seattle ahead for good.
At Utah, Karl Malone scored 20 points as the Jazz tied a franchise record for home wins with a 106-93 victory over the Golden State Warriors.
Chris Morris scored 15 points and Jeff Hornacek added 12 for the Jazz, who improved to 37-3 at the Delta Centre, matching their 37 home wins in the 1991-92 season.
Utah can break its record at home Saturday against Minnesota.
Chris Mullin scored 19 points and Latrell Sprewell added 14 for the Warriors, losers of 10 of their last 11 road games.
In Vancouver, Rasheed Wallace scored 25 points to lead the Portland Trail Blazers to a 105-73 rout the Grizzlies.
Arvydas Sabonis added 15 and nine rebounds and Rumeal Robinson had 14 points and seven assists for Portland, which has won its last two games by a combined 76 points.
Anthony Peeler had 16 points to lead Vancouver (13-68), which will not be able to to match its inaugural-season record of 15-67.
Portland led 69-59 after three quarters and busted the game wide open by outscoring Vancouver 36-15 over the final 12 minutes.
